summary: Made SidekickMenu search opt-in for v2.0.0. UI/SidekickMenu/SidekickMenu.tsx: searchEnabled now defaults to false (the existing `searchEnabled && !effectiveRailCollapsed` guard unmounts the input entirely, so nothing invisible is focusable, and the null-guarded autofocus effect no-ops). Added a small effect that dispatches SET_SEARCH_TERM "" when search is turned off while a term is active, so the menu is never left filtered by an invisible query. Search enabled keeps every 1.7.0 path unchanged (placeholder, autofocus, icon, matching, ordering, numbered shortcuts, empty list). types.ts documents searchEnabled as opt-in with default false. Updated every existing search test to pass searchEnabled (none deleted or skipped) and added tests for the hidden default, false/undefined, opt-in rendering, prop-flip term reset, autofocus, rail collapse, no-match empty state, non-persistence, plus release metadata. Bumped package.json to 2.0.0, added the v2.0.0 breaking-changes entry with the searchEnabled={true} migration and ToC item, and updated README/docs/features/docs/examples to present search as opt-in. docs/api.md and docs/configuration.md were intentionally left to the other build slice (out of this step's declared parts) and remain in the repo's pre-existing state for that step. Build passes. Focused suite: 55/55. Full suite: 211 passed, 2 failed in Styles/SidekickMenu.theme.test.ts only - both are pre-existing Windows/CRLF regex failures in an untouched file (the working-tree Styles/SidekickMenu.module.css is CRLF while those tests read it expecting LF), unrelated to this change. Finished the documentation slice of the search opt-in change. docs/api.md now lists searchEnabled with default false and describes it as opt-in (pass true to render the input). docs/configuration.md now shows searchEnabled: false in its defaults snippet and its search section says search is off unless enabled, with a searchEnabled={true} example; both pages keep their previous/next links. Extended the R4 tests in SidekickMenu.test.tsx to cover api.md and configuration.md (default false, opt-in wording, defaults snippet, prev/next navigation) and to assert the README's first working example contains no searchEnabled. Build and targeted tests pass; the full suite has only the two pre-existing Windows CRLF failures in the untouched Styles/SidekickMenu.theme.test.ts.
